comment: Cross-business imports the WebUI role check accepts deliberately. Plan §5.3.2 lets a feature import another feature's *approved public* interface; a feature's contracts are its published surface and need no entry, but any other cross-business edge does. Each entry names both files so a reviewer sees the exact dependency, and a `reason` so the next migration can judge whether it should survive. An entry that no longer matches a measured edge fails the check (see `roleRule`), so the list shrinks as ownership transfers instead of accumulating.

entries.reason: The transcript renders the interaction business's plan decision card as the response surface of a plan turn (plan 5.2 transcript row: uses the interaction answer API). The card is that business's own UI. T05 moved the interactions business into `client/features/interactions/` and the path was re-pointed then; the entry goes when interactions publishes the delivery/decision card as a public surface instead of a peer's UI module.

Sessions publishes its action-request builders as a public module, so the transcript's message actions and the composer build session commands (fork / edit / rewind) through the owner's published command shape instead of a peer's private module. The `.public` suffix is a publication marker; the builders themselves are unchanged.

Archiving or deleting a session clears that session's Composer draft, so the workflow calls the composer store's own clear. Repointed when T13 moved the composer owner into its feature home; the entry goes when composer publishes a public clear command.

Workspace publishes the project-name rule as a public module, so the rail and the composer's project row read the owner's derivation instead of a peer's private module. The `.public` suffix is a publication marker; the rule itself is unchanged.

Workspace publishes the project-name rule as a public module, so the rail and the composer's project row read the owner's derivation instead of a peer's private module. The `.public` suffix is a publication marker; the rule itself is unchanged.

The user menu opens the settings modal. It is an Account surface opening the settings composition; T12 moved the settings files into their feature home and re-pointed this entry. It goes when Settings publishes the open command as a public contract.

The workspace composer composes the review owner: the panels read one snapshot, and the review half is a peer business's owner. T11's acceptance says compose T10's review APIs rather than reimplementing review policy, and the owner factory is what there is to compose; the entry goes when review publishes a composition contract.

The review settings page lists the sessions it can review. Sessions publishes the catalogue state shape and its page selectors as a public module, so the page resolves the same catalogue the rail renders instead of reaching into a peer's private application module. The `.public` suffix is a publication marker; the read is unchanged.

Transcript publishes its markdown renderer as a public presentation module, so the plan decision card and the workspace panel render through the owner's published renderer instead of a peer's private one. The `.public` suffix is a publication marker; the renderer and what it produces are unchanged.
The review settings page renders the worktree surface's grouping for the sessions it reviews. Reviewed peer edge until Sessions publishes that projection as a public contract.

The workspace panel hosts the terminal tab, so it measures the terminal grid. The plan keeps the terminal presented inside the workspace; the entry goes when T15 gives the terminal its own presentation attachment.

The transcript's diff card mounts the review business's turn-review binding to read a turn's diff. Before T10 the binding sat in `client/bindings/`, which the role rules classify as a home with no business, so the edge was not cross-business; moving it into the review business's own `bindings/` makes it one. Reviewed peer edge: the card renders review state, it does not own it, and the entry goes when review publishes the turn-diff read as a public contract the transcript can consume without its binding (T10).

The same binding, asked only whether the runtime offers turn diffs at all, so the card can be hidden rather than rendered empty. Same edge and same retirement as the DiffCard entry: review publishes the capability read as a public contract and this goes with it (T10).

The settings dialog renders the worktree surface's grouping for the archived-session settings page (the same projection the review settings page reads). Both files sat in current homes before T12 moved the dialog into the settings feature home, so the edge was not judged; reviewed peer edge until Sessions publishes the worktree projection as a public contract.

Review publishes its settings page as a public screen contract, so the settings dialog composes Review's published surface as one of its tabs instead of reaching into a peer's private component. The `.public` suffix is a publication marker; the page and the reads it performs are unchanged.

The settings dialog reads the account owner's snapshot through the account business's own binding (account status, sign-in and quota are setting-page resources that Account owns). Reviewed peer edge until Account publishes the status read as a public contract, or the dialog takes it as an injected view (T12's composition).

The archived-session settings page lists sessions from the sessions catalogue, the same read the review settings page makes. Sessions publishes that read as a public module; the `.public` suffix is a publication marker and the read is unchanged.

The usage/model-source screen shows the account's quota and credential status, read through the account business's own binding. Reviewed peer edge until Account publishes the status read as a public contract.

The screen derives the active source badge, the provider header draft and the reset label through the models projection. Reviewed peer edge until Models publishes that derivation (T03 owns the models surface).

Models publishes its provider form as a public screen contract, so the settings screen embeds the provider CRUD Models owns rather than importing a peer's private component. The `.public` suffix is a publication marker; the form and its commands are unchanged.

The screen hosts the Models provider editor above its custom-tab branch, which is what keeps a draft and its tested flag alive across a source-tab switch (plan §5.5, §5.7 LC-4). The editor's policy stays Models': the screen only holds the instance and renders its snapshot. Reviewed peer edge until Models publishes the editor handle as a public binding surface.

The session-keyed interaction owner applies the same session-scoped interaction commands after a questionnaire settles, for the same reason as the coordinator entry above. Reviewed peer edge until sessions publishes the command view as a public contract.

Transcript publishes its markdown renderer as a public presentation module, so the plan decision card and the workspace panel render through the owner's published renderer instead of a peer's private one. The `.public` suffix is a publication marker; the renderer and what it produces are unchanged.

The composer's thinking trigger renders the models business's thinking-control projection (the control's vocabulary is Models', plan 5.2's models row). Reviewed peer edge until Models publishes that read.

The composer's project row hosts the workspace business's directory browser for the picker; T13 moved that row out of WebuiComposer into its own unit and the edge moved with it. Reviewed peer edge: the surface is Workspace's and the row only places it; it goes when Workspace publishes the picker.

The composer types its own plugin props (the catalogue object it reads from the owner and the installed-plugin list it holds) with the plugins business's Composer-facing shapes. Reviewed peer edge until Plugins publishes them from its contracts.

The composer's `+` menu lists the plugins business's Composer-facing catalogue (installed plugins and runtime skills) through the read model T08 published; T13 moved the menu out of WebuiComposer into its own unit and the edge moved with it. Reviewed peer edge until Plugins publishes it from its contracts.

The composer lists the child sessions of the session it composes for by resolving the sessions business's catalogue through its own selector. Sessions publishes the catalogue state shape and its page selectors as a public module, so the composer reads the owner's published read model rather than a peer's private application module. The `.public` suffix is a publication marker; the read is unchanged.

The composer reads the account business's live status to guard its own model scope against another session's value; before T13 that status arrived as an RPC prop the shell relayed. Reviewed peer edge until Account publishes a binding the shell can mount.
The composer types its sink against the interaction coordinator, the interaction view of the turn writer surface. Reviewed peer edge until interactions publishes the coordinator as a public contract.
The composer asks whether the selected model is a token-plan model, the same read the rail's chip makes. Reviewed peer edge until Models publishes the plan read.

Goal publishes its owner bindings as a public module, so the composer mounts the goal business's own binding rather than reaching into a peer's private one. The `.public` suffix is a publication marker; the binding and the owner it reads are unchanged, and the owner stays the application's — a screen unmount still owns no goal state.

Interactions publishes its owner binding as a public module, so the composer mounts the interactions business's own binding rather than reaching into a peer's private one. The `.public` suffix is a publication marker; the binding is unchanged, and the owner stays the application's with no reader installed from a view.

The composer inspects a session's status to decide whether it is still running. Turn publishes that normalisation as a public module, so the composer reads the owner's published status contract instead of re-deriving the wire enum from a peer's private projection. The `.public` suffix is a publication marker; the rule is unchanged.
The composer renders the account usage label in its context chip; the label derivation is Account's. Reviewed peer edge until Account publishes that projection.

Goal publishes its banner as a public screen contract, so the composer places the goal business's published surface above its own field. The `.public` suffix is a publication marker; publishing the component does not transfer its business truth — the banner still renders the goal the Goal owner holds.
The composer places the interactions business's permission/questionnaire panel. Reviewed peer edge until interactions publishes the panel as a public surface.
The composer mounts the models business's picker: model choice is Models' owner and Models' surface. Reviewed peer edge until Models publishes the picker.
The composer reads the models business's thinking-control rules for its toolbar control. Reviewed peer edge until Models publishes them.

Transcript publishes its output-error surface as a public screen contract, so the composer renders the transcript business's published surface under its field. The `.public` suffix is a publication marker; the component and what it renders are unchanged.

Sessions publishes its action-request builders as a public module, so the transcript's message actions and the composer build session commands (fork / edit / rewind) through the owner's published command shape instead of a peer's private module. The `.public` suffix is a publication marker; the builders themselves are unchanged.

Workspace publishes the project-name rule as a public module, so the rail and the composer's project row read the owner's derivation instead of a peer's private module. The `.public` suffix is a publication marker; the rule itself is unchanged.

The indicator shows the token plan when the selected model is one. This is Composer's existing read of Models' plan projection, now also declared for the surface that renders it; the edge goes when Models publishes the plan read as a public contract (the path was re-pointed when the models business moved into features/models/ in T03; the edge itself predates this move and is unchanged).

The indicator shows account usage. Composer's existing read of Account's usage projection, now also declared for the surface that renders it; the edge goes when Account publishes the usage read as a public contract (T09 owns the account lifetime).
